records.description: Terra-Gen develops, owns and operates utility-scale wind, solar and battery-storage assets across the United States. Public disclosures through July 2026 describe approximately 4.2 GW of gross operating capacity, 5.6 GWh of storage, 34 sites and a roughly 16 GW development pipeline. Terra-Gen Power Holdings II, LLC is the parent platform, Terra-Gen, LLC is the operating business and individual project SPVs remain subordinate assets. Current legal ownership is 50% through Igneo Infrastructure Partners' Global Diversified Infrastructure Fund chain and 50% through Masdar's acquisition chain. ArcLight formed the platform in 2007, Global Infrastructure Partners invested in 2009, Energy Capital Partners acquired it in 2015 and used a 2021 continuation vehicle for its retained 50% before Masdar closed its purchase on October 1, 2024. Pantheon Infrastructure Plc committed to a Terra-Gen-specific co-investment through an Igneo-managed vehicle in June 2026, but closing, funding, the security and stake were not publicly confirmed; Igneo remains recorded at 50% pending evidence. No later corporate ownership change or signed exit was identified through August 19, 2026.

milestones.event: ArcLight formed Terra-Gen from renewable-generation assets acquired from Caithness.
Igneo's Global Diversified Infrastructure Fund closed an initial 40% investment and increased its Terra-Gen interest to 50%; ECP transferred its retained 50% into a continuation vehicle.
Masdar announced an agreement to acquire Energy Capital Partners' 50% Terra-Gen stake while Igneo retained its 50% interest.
Masdar completed its 50% acquisition from Energy Capital Partners, leaving Terra-Gen owned 50% by Masdar and 50% by Igneo's GDIF chain.
Global Infrastructure Partners agreed to invest through convertible preferred securities representing up to a 40% interest in Terra-Gen.
Energy Capital Partners III acquired Terra-Gen, ending the ArcLight and Global Infrastructure Partners ownership periods.
Pantheon Infrastructure announced a Terra-Gen-specific co-investment commitment through an Igneo-managed vehicle; closing, funding and the resulting stake were not publicly confirmed.

records.description: Mesteño Wind Project is a 201.6 MW onshore wind facility in Starr County, Texas, commonly described as a 202 MW project. The facility comprises 56 Vestas V136-3.6 MW turbines, began commercial operation in 2019 and participates in the ERCOT market. InfraRed Capital Partners acquired the project company, Mesteno Windpower, LLC, from Duke Energy through Mesteno Aggregator LLC on May 29, 2024. Current regulatory records show InfraRed Energy Transition Fund A LP holding 3.48% directly in the aggregator and InfraRed Energy Transition Fund B LP holding 96.52% indirectly through Mesteno HoldCo LLC. The two positions together represent 100% InfraRed-controlled ownership. No later owner exit or signed ownership change was identified through September 1, 2026.

records.description: Longroad Energy Holdings, LLC develops, owns and operates utility-scale wind, solar and battery-storage projects across the United States. The company was founded in 2016 and serves utilities, corporations and wholesale power markets through a development-to-ownership model that combines contracted offtake, asset management and project-level financing. Current economic ownership is held by Infratil, New Zealand Super Fund, Munich Re and Longroad management. Infratil reported a 42.5% economic interest at March 31, 2026, while its current investment page reports 42.0%; the same page reports New Zealand Super Fund at 34.8%, Longroad management at 13.0% and Munich Re at 9.7%. Morrison manages or advises the Infratil and New Zealand Super Fund investments but is not itself recorded as a beneficial owner. MEAG manages Munich Re's interest through MR Hunu LP. No later company-level owner exit or signed ownership change was identified through September 1, 2026.

milestones.event: Infratil and New Zealand Super Fund closed their investment in Longroad at 45% each, with management holding 10%; Morrison managed the two institutional investments.
Longroad announced a US$500 million equity round led by MEAG for Munich Re alongside additional Infratil and New Zealand Super Fund capital.
The MEAG-led financing closed, adding Munich Re as a beneficial owner through MR Hunu LP while Infratil, New Zealand Super Fund and management remained invested.

records.description: 38 Degrees North develops, owns, and operates distributed generation, community solar, battery storage, and related sustainable infrastructure assets. Its end markets include communities, development partners, capital providers, utilities, and commercial counterparties seeking distributed clean-energy solutions. The operating model combines development and ownership of physical energy assets with flexible capital partnerships, making it more infrastructure oriented than a software-only platform. Public materials describe a focus on community solar, distributed generation, and storage, and a July 2025 funding announcement stated that the company had raised more than $230 million of corporate growth capital and acquired U.S. Light Energy's 250 MW-plus pipeline. Kimmeridge made a growth equity investment alongside Climate Adaptive Infrastructure in 2025.

records.description: Port Arthur LNG is a two-phase liquefied-natural-gas export development in Jefferson County, Texas. Phase 1 comprises two liquefaction trains with approximately 13 Mtpa of nameplate capacity and is owned indirectly by KKR Denali (42%), Sempra Infrastructure Partners (28%) and ConocoPhillips (30%). Phase 2 adds approximately 13 Mtpa across two further trains and reached FID in September 2025; its direct legal members hold 50.1%, 40.0% and 9.9% interests, with KKR participating within the 40% member's parent consortium. The project is distinct from Sempra Infrastructure Partners, whose separate KKR-led platform transaction remained pending as of the latest verification.

records.description: Dames Point Jacksonville LLC is the local operating and concession entity associated with JAXPORT's 158-acre Dames Point container terminal and adjacent intermodal container transfer facility in Jacksonville, Florida. The business handles container, stevedoring, crane, yard and rail-transfer activity for ocean carriers, cargo owners and military users under long-term port rights. Ceres acquired the former TraPac Jacksonville entity in 2022; Macquarie retained the renamed local SPV when the broader Ceres platform was sold to Carrix, then sold the Jacksonville business and assets separately to JAXPORT in November 2023. JAXPORT is the current owner and SSA is the contract operator, not an equity owner.

The business handles container, stevedoring, crane, yard and rail-transfer activity for ocean carriers, cargo owners and military users under long-term port rights. Ceres acquired the former TraPac Jacksonville entity in 2022; Macquarie retained the renamed local SPV when the broader Ceres platform was sold to Carrix, then sold the Jacksonville business and assets separately to JAXPORT in November 2023. JAXPORT is the current owner and SSA is the contract operator, not an equity owner.

milestones.event: Macquarie Infrastructure Partners III acquired 49% of the broader Ceres Terminals platform; this was platform history rather than the local Jacksonville entry date.
Macquarie Infrastructure Partners III increased its interest in the broader Ceres Terminals platform to 100%.
Ceres acquired 100% of TraPac Jacksonville and began the 20-year terminal and ICTF lease, establishing Macquarie's local Jacksonville ownership period.
Macquarie agreed to sell the broader Ceres platform to Carrix while expressly retaining Jacksonville; the local SPV was renamed Dames Point Jacksonville LLC and moved under Bluefin.
JAXPORT acquired the Dames Point Jacksonville business and assets; SSA subsequently operated the terminal under contract.
